key_insight: The paper shows that not all ways of using demonstration quality help equally in VLA pretraining: the best gains come from choosing the right combination of weighting, filtering, or conditioning rather than simply using more data. It benchmarks these strategies across different reward definitions and label granularities to identify what actually transfers to downstream tasks.
problem_solved: It addresses how to exploit quality signals from suboptimal human demonstrations during vision-language-action pretraining so that models improve after fine-tuning on target tasks, instead of wasting noisy or low-value data.
method: Compare three quality-use strategies during pretraining: weighting demonstrations, filtering demonstrations, and conditioning the model on quality tags.
Evaluate these strategies across multiple reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations.

Measure transfer to 24 target tasks while matching demonstration counts and training budgets within each VLA, and test the effects of pretraining data size plus quality tags during fine-tuning and inference.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a practical playbook for making pretraining data more useful without increasing budget. It helps decide whether to weight, filter, or condition on quality labels to get better downstream performance from VLA systems.

paper_title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
paper_authors: Mingxuan Yan, Litian Gong, Dihong Huang, Zhixu Li, Tianyu Zhang
